audit_findings.title: Convertible notes are counted as both debt and equity
audit_findings.magnitude: 5.479325 million excess shares; denominator is 10.4% larger than the consistent debt-treatment denominator of 52.515023 million shares; base value would compute to approximately $23.48 per share instead of $21.25
audit_findings.mechanism: The conversion shares inflate the share denominator even though interest remains in owner earnings and the $345 million principal is treated as debt rather than deducted in the equity bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: Conversions of the 2029 Convertible Notes will be settled in cash up to the aggregate principal amount of the 2029 Convertible Notes to be converted, and cash, shares of common stock or a combination of cash and shares of common stock, at the Company’s election, with respect to the remainder, if any, of the Company’s conversion obligation in excess of the aggregate principal amount.
audit_findings.explanation: This is a demonstrated internal inconsistency. Removing the conversion shares while retaining the debt treatment raises per-share value enough for the base value to move from below the $23.18 market price to slightly above it, so it can change the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Rerun all scenarios using either 52.515023 million shares with interest retained and principal treated as debt context, or a conversion branch that adjusts interest, cash principal settlement and only the applicable excess-value shares.

audit_findings.title: BAQSIMI contingent consideration may be an omitted senior cash claim
audit_findings.magnitude: $100.0 million accrued and due in the third quarter of 2026, equal to approximately $1.72 per valuation share; up to a further $475.0 million remains contingent
audit_findings.mechanism: The valuation adds June 2026 cash and short-term investments but does not subtract the $100 million milestone payable or explicitly include future milestone cash payments in projected owner earnings.
audit_findings.evidence: The terms of our Purchase Agreement with Lilly require us to make future sales-based milestone payments aggregating up to $575.0 million based on achievement of specified net sales amounts.
audit_findings.explanation: The June 2026 filing resolves part of the earlier possibility: a $100 million milestone was triggered and recorded as a liability. Deducting it would reduce base value from $21.25 to approximately $19.53 per share. The timing and probability of the remaining $475 million cannot yet be established, but the demonstrated $100 million omission is independently material.
audit_findings.action: Rerun the bridge with the accrued $100 million deducted, or use post-payment cash without a second deduction; separately model the remaining milestones from contract-year sales projections and payment terms.

audit_findings.title: Known capital-spending step-up is absent from the mechanical OE forecast
audit_findings.mechanism: Higher maintenance, compliance or growth capital expenditures would reduce forecast owner earnings below the mechanical growth path based on FY2025 owner earnings.
audit_findings.evidence: Our future capital expenditures include projects to upgrade, expand, and improve our manufacturing facilities in the United States and China, including a significant increase in capital expenditures over the next few years.
audit_findings.explanation: Management forecasts a significant capital-spending increase, but no filed amount or schedule establishes the incremental required spending. Actual capital expenditures were $34.9 million in 2025 and $18.1 million in the first half of 2026, which does not yet demonstrate the forecast step-up or its maintenance component. This is therefore a forward-looking exposure rather than a presently quantifiable valuation error.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the project-by-project capital plan, timing and committed amounts; classify maintenance, compliance and optional expansion spending, then rerun each growth scenario with the required expenditures deducted.

audit_findings.title: A recurring lease cost began immediately after the anchor year
audit_findings.magnitude: approximately $3.6 million first-year pretax rent, escalating 3.25% annually; the initial annual rent equals 5.1% of the $70.9 million OE anchor
audit_findings.mechanism: The lease cost begins in 2026 and reduces forecast owner earnings, while the FY2025 anchor contains none of it and the lease liability is not deducted in the bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: The Company did not recognize any lease expense and has no ROU assets or lease liability recognized as of December 31, 2025, given that the lease commenced on January 1, 2026.
audit_findings.explanation: The cost and commencement are demonstrated, and its initial scale exceeds the bull value's 4.3% premium to the $23.18 market price. It is therefore reasonably capable of changing the conclusion, although the net effect could be smaller if the facility produces incremental earnings or avoids other costs.
audit_findings.action: Rerun 2026 onward owner earnings with the full rent and escalation, net of specifically supported incremental earnings and avoided costs; do not also deduct the lease liability if rent is fully included.

audit_findings.title: The anchor retains a material litigation charge that may be nonrecurring
audit_findings.magnitude: $23.1 million pretax, equal to 32.6% of the $70.9 million OE anchor
audit_findings.mechanism: The cash settlement reduced FY2025 owner earnings, which is used as the sole forecast anchor; normalization would increase the anchor after allowing for taxes and recurring litigation costs.
audit_findings.evidence: The increase in general and administrative expense was primarily related to a legal settlement, which increased expenses by $23.1 million.
audit_findings.explanation: The charge and payment are demonstrated, while whether and how much to normalize remains a judgment. Its scale is plainly material: even a partial justified add-back could materially raise every scenario. The current valuation is conservative if the personal-injury settlement is exceptional rather than representative.
audit_findings.action: Confirm the settlement cash outflow is included in the OE calculation, determine the applicable tax effect, establish a supportable recurring legal and product-liability allowance, and rerun the scenarios using only the justified net add-back.

audit_findings.title: Some cash added dollar-for-dollar may be unavailable to the parent
audit_findings.magnitude: $15.8 million maximum identified foreign-subsidiary cash exposure, approximately $0.27 per share and 1.3% of base equity value
audit_findings.mechanism: Any unavailable or impaired foreign cash would reduce the cash and short-term-investment addition in the equity bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: Cash or cash equivalents held at foreign subsidiaries are not available to fund the parent company’s operations in the United States.
audit_findings.explanation: Even excluding the entire filed $15.8 million foreign cash balance would reduce base value only from $21.25 to approximately $20.98 per share. That does not change the relationship to the $23.18 market price or the $14.87 buy-below threshold, so the identified balance is not material to the present conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile the $290.123 million bridge addition by entity and instrument and document restrictions or repatriation costs; rerun only if additional unavailable balances or costs materially exceed the identified $15.8 million.
